title: Twin Networks for Counterfactuals
description: Balke and Pearl's twin-network method computes counterfactuals by duplicating the causal model — one copy for the observed world, one for the hypothetical — with both sharing the same exogenous background variables. Abduction updates the shared background from what was observed; prediction then runs the hypothetical forward.

demo.code:
import random
random.seed(1001)
x_obs=1.0; x_cf=0.0; n=500
# structural model: U ~ N(0,1); Y = 2*X + U. Observe X=x_obs; counterfactual: X had been x_cf.
U=[random.gauss(0,1) for _ in range(n)]
Y_obs=[2*x_obs+u for u in U]
Y_cf=[2*x_cf+u for u in U]
eff=sum(y_cf-y_o for y_cf,y_o in zip(Y_cf,Y_obs))/n
print(f"observed_mean={sum(Y_obs)/n:.3f} counterfactual_mean={sum(Y_cf)/n:.3f}")
print(f"individual_effect={eff:.3f} (truth={(2*(x_cf-x_obs)):.3f})")
print("DEMO_OK")
demo.note: Runnable demo program verified by execution during the database build.

architecture: The builder clones the structural model into factual and counterfactual copies joined at the background nodes. Evidence conditions the background distribution, the hypothetical intervention is applied to the clone, and the query is read off the counterfactual copy.
implementation_status: Public method, established (Balke & Pearl 1994). Prototype validated in this build (executed 2026-10-21).

acceptance_tests.test: Observed evidence correctly conditions the background

provenance: Balke, A. & Pearl, J. (1994). Probabilistic evaluation of counterfactual queries. AAAI. Public record.
